title.narrative: Provision of life-saving and sustainable WASH services to undeserved drought displaced affected populations and host communities in Afgooye district

description.narrative:
ltpgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtSomalia is facing an unprecedented sixth consecutive season of below-average- April to June 2023 rains. The Protracted drought has claimed the lives and livelihoods of many. An estimated 8.25 million people require humanitarian assistance. According to FSNAU’s 2022 Post Dyer assessment, the food and nutrition situation remains critical in several districts and is expected to deteriorate further between January to June 2023 due to an anticipated sixth consecutive below-average rainfall season from April to June 2023. The risk of famine (IPC Phase 5) remains credible through at least June in agro pastoral areas of Afgooyenbspdistrict, the number of people affected by drought has more than doubled since the beginning of 2022. As per the 2023 HNO, drought induced displacement has increased fivefold since the beginning of 2022 with more than 1.3 million people displaced. Five regions including lower shabelle have received the biggest numbers of newly displaced people.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtThe cumulative effects of consecutive below-average rainy seasons have resulted in a sharp increase in humanitarian needs across all sectors including food security, health, nutrition, WASH, protection and CCCM. Water shortages are at critical levels exposing vulnerable people to additional risks. According to the HNO, eight million people (62 per cent of whom are children) need immediate WASH assistance. About 1,800 out of 8,200 water sources are nonfunctional and require urgent rehabilitation. Water prices are six times higher than at the beginning of 2022 and are likely to remain high. Increasing food insecurity and declining water availability and quality have led to outbreaks of AWD/Cholera in many parts of the country. In January 2023, a total of 217 new cholera cases have been reported from 23 drought affected districts, with most of the cases reported in three locations including Afgoye. As the drought intensives throughout Somalia, water becomes an essential and very expensive commodity to the pastoralists, agro-pastoralists as well as the vulnerable IDPs in Afgoyenbspdistrict.
